The bullish narrative put fair value at CA$5.09. It was built on the idea that low emission Tier IV fleets and deeper long-term contracts in Argentina would support stronger margins as older equipment left the field and more work shifted to modernized spreads.

The bearish view saw fair value at CA$3.55. It focused on decarbonization risk, expecting weaker oilfield service demand and arguing that high fixed costs and heavy capital spending could keep pressure on free cash flow and profitability.

The lesson is simple. When a thesis leans on margin improvement, track the net margin line in each report and compare it with the original narrative, not just with revenue or headline earnings.
